arxiv-2102-01112.title: Phase-coherent thermoelectricity and non-equilibrium Josephson current in Andreev interferometers
arxiv-2102-01112.creator: Mikhail S. Kalenkov, Andrei D. Zaikin
arxiv-2102-01112.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mikhail S. Kalenkov, Andrei D. Zaikin. We develop a detailed theory describing a non-trivial interplay between non-equilibrium effects and long-range quantum coherence in superconducting hybrid nanostructures exposed to a temperature gradient. We establish a direct relation between thermoelectric and Josephson effects in such structures and demonstrate that at temperatures exceeding the Thouless energy of our device both phase-coherent thermoelectric signal and the supercurrent may be strongly enhanced due to non-equilibrium low energy quasiparticles propagating across the system without any significant phase relaxation.

arxiv-2512-14463.title: Super-Heisenberg-limited Sensing via Collective Subradiance in Waveguide QED
arxiv-2512-14463.creator: Xin Wang, Zeyang Liao
arxiv-2512-14463.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xin Wang, Zeyang Liao. We explore the quantum-metrological potential of subwavelength-spaced emitter arrays coupled to a one-dimensional nanophotonic waveguide. In this system, strong dipole–dipole interactions profoundly modify the collective optical response, leading to the emergence of ultranarrow subradiant resonances. Through an eigenmode analysis of the effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, we derive a universal scaling law for the decay rate of the most subradiant state, which exhibits an N − 3 N^{-3} scaling with even-odd oscillatory behavior in the deep-subwavelength regime.

arxiv-2601-19988.description: Abstract Optically addressable spins at material surfaces have represented a long-standing ambition in quantum sensing, providing atomic resolution and quantum-limited sensitivity. However, they are constrained by a finite depth at which the quantum spins can be stabilized. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid molecular-2D architecture that realizes quantum spin sensors directly on top of the surface.

pmc-13483046.title: Molecular mechanisms of mitochondrial Ca2+ exchanger NCLX
pmc-13483046.creator: Li Zhang, Yan Han, Weizhong Zeng, Jing Xue, Yan Wang, Youxing Jiang
pmc-13483046.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mitochondrial Ca²⁺ homeostasis is maintained through coordinated influx and efflux processes, with NCLX long recognized as the primary Ca²⁺ extruder operating via Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchange. Here, we report cryo-EM structures of rat NCLX in cytosolic-facing occluded and open states. The central transmembrane (TM) domain of NCLX comprises ten helices arranged in two inverted, structurally similar halves, with two α-repeats forming a central ion-binding pocket. Peripheral TMs 1 and 6 are loosely associated with the core and likely mediate alternative access to this site.

uslaw-usc-t20-s80q13.title: 20 U.S.C. § 80q–13 — Grants by Secretary of the Interior to assist Indian organizations with respect to renovation and repair of museum facilities and exhibit facilities
uslaw-usc-t20-s80q13.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t20-s80q13.description: United States Code, Title 20 (Education); Chapter 3 (Smithsonian Institution, National Museums And Art Galleries); Subchapter XIII (National Museum Of The American Indian). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Grants The Secretary of the Interior may make grants to Indian organizations, including Indian tribes, museums, cultural centers, educational institutions, libraries, and archives, for renovation and repair of museum facilities and exhibit facilities.
